title: Association between polygenic liability to depression and lifetime depression in at-risk adolescents
title_zh: 多基因易感性与高危青少年终身抑郁的关联
abstract: Abstract Internalising symptoms including depression, anxiety and somatic symptoms in adolescence are common. They can be transient, but they can also persist and progress to major depressive disorder (MDD) Polygenic risk scores for major depression (MD-PGS) may help identify which symptomatic adolescents are at greatest risk of later disorder. In a mega-analysis of two longitudinal population-based cohorts from Brisbane, Australia, we investigated whether polygenic liability to depression improves risk stratification among adolescents with elevated internalising symptoms. Internalising symptoms were assessed at age 14, lifetime MDD was assessed in young adulthood using the Composite International Diagnostic Interview, and MD-PGS were generated using summary statistics from the latest Psychiatric Genomics Consortium major depression genome-wide association study, excluding Australian cohorts. Analyses focused on comparisons between individuals in the top decile of risk and those in the remaining 90% of each cohort. A total of 302 cases with lifetime MDD and 1693 controls were included. Compared with adolescents outside the highest decile of internalising symptoms, those in the top decile at age 14 had a more than two-fold increased odds of lifetime MDD (OR = 2.56, 95% CI 1.92–3.49, p = 5.4 × 10 -10 ). Individuals in the top decile of MD-PGS also showed increased odds of lifetime MDD compared with the remaining 90% (OR = 3.45, 95% CI 2.53–4.71, p = 4.4 × 10 − ¹⁵). Adolescents who were simultaneously in the top decile of both internalising symptoms and MD-PGS had an approximately eight-fold increased odds of lifetime MDD compared with individuals outside the top decile for both risk factors (OR = 8.58, 95% CI 4.04–18.26, p = 1.2 × 10 − ⁵). These findings indicate that polygenic risk scores for depression may have particular clinical utility for stratifying risk among adolescents already presenting with elevated internalising symptoms, identifying a subgroup at very high risk for later major depressive disorder.
abstract_zh: 摘要：青少年期的内化症状，包括抑郁、焦虑和躯体症状，十分常见。它们可能是短暂的，也可能持续并进展为重性抑郁障碍（MDD）。重性抑郁的多基因风险评分（MD‑PGS）可能有助于识别哪些出现症状的青少年在后期发展为障碍的风险最高。在澳大利亚布里斯班的两组纵向人群队列的宏观分析中，我们研究了多基因抑郁易感性是否能改善对内化症状升高青少年的风险分层。内化症状在14岁时评估，终身MDD在成年早期使用综合国际诊断访谈评估，MD‑PGS使用最新精神病学基因组学联盟重性抑郁全基因组关联研究的摘要统计生成，排除澳大利亚队列。分析聚焦于风险最高十分位与其余90%个体的比较。共纳入302例终身MDD病例和1693例对照。与非最高十分位内化症状的青少年相比，14岁时处于最高十分位的青少年终身MDD的风险增加超过两倍（OR = 2.56，95% CI 1.92–3.49，p = 5.4 × 10⁻¹⁰）。MD‑PGS最高十分位的个体与其余90%相比也显示出终身MDD风险增加（OR = 3.45，95% CI 2.53–4.71，p = 4.4 × 10⁻¹⁵）。同时处于内化症状和MD‑PGS最高十分位的青少年，其终身MDD风险约为非两者最高十分位个体的八倍（OR = 8.58，95% CI 4.04–18.26，p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵）。这些发现表明，抑郁的多基因风险评分可能在临床上具有特别的价值，用于对已出现内化症状升高的青少年进行风险分层，识别出后期发展为重性抑郁障碍的极高风险亚群。
